catalog_quote: Stress in South Sulawesi languages usually occurs on the penultimate syllable. In such cases it is not marked in the word lists. Where stress deviates from the normal pattern or where stress may be unclear due to double vocoids, etc., it is marked with an apostrophe preceding the stressed syllable.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (216 pp., ANU open-repository scan with text) and rendered p.102 to an image: the Appendix E "SYMBOLS" block reads, under the apostrophe symbol, "Stress in South Sulawesi languages usually occurs on the penultimate syllable. In such cases it is not marked in the word lists. Where stress deviates from the normal pattern or where stress may be unclear due to double vocoids, etc., it is marked with an apostrophe preceding the stressed syllable." -- verbatim as quoted. Two small corrections to the report: (1) the printed page number on that page is 94, not 93 (the "93" in the text is the foot of the preceding classification-tree page); p.102 is right. (2) The single apostrophe-marked Kal…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Family-level generalisation applied to the authors' own Kalumpang wordlist (collected Jan 1983 by F. Dawson from two Kalumpang speakers): stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the word; in the Kalumpang column the only stress-marked item is 'kaaun 'wind' (stress on the first of two adjacent identical vowels, i.e. a double-vocoid case where the count of syllables is unclear); every other Kalumpang item is unmarked, i.e. penultimate.
new_statements.exceptions: 'usually'; deviations and double-vocoid cases marked with an apostrophe. For Kalumpang, one marked item ('kaaun 'wind', p. 115); the note on Selayar antepenultimate stress (p. 96) concerns Selayar, not Kalumpang.
new_statements.domain_note: Citation-form words in a 200-item comparative wordlist; the statement is made for South Sulawesi languages as a group, not for Kalumpang specifically, and rests on survey wordlists rather than a phonological analysis. Confidence low for that reason.
new_statements.identity_note: The Grimes & Grimes 1987 Kalumpang list is a single village list ('Kalumpang', collected Jan 1983 by F. Dawson; informants Samuel Mangandu and Abraham Kambuno); dialect not specified (Valkama 1987 reports it agrees 85% with his kota Kalumpang list and counts eight dialects: Karataun, Bone Hau, Mangki/E'da, Mablei etc.). The stress statement itself is a blanket one for all South Sulawesi languages in the survey, not a Kalumpang-specific analysis. Van der Veen 1929 calls the language Mangki'sch (Makki); Badan Bahasa's Peta Bahasa lists Kalumpang as a dialect (Karataun, Bonehau) rather than a language. Glottocode kalu1247 covers the whole cluster.

sources.citation: OLAC. 2025. Resources in and about the Kalumpang language (kli). language-archives.org.
sources.note: Bibliographic record only: lists no language description of Kalumpang beyond Glottolog/Ethnologue/LINGUIST List pointers and Strømme 1987 (survey). Confirms the absence of any published phonology or grammar in the OLAC aggregate.

sources.citation: Laskowske, Thomas V. 2006. The Seko languages of South Sulawesi: a reconstruction. Paper, 10-ICAL, Puerto Princesa. SIL.
sources.note: 'Stress is penultimate' is stated for the Seko languages only. Kalumpang (Klp, Bone Hau and Karama dialects, from unpublished 488-item SIL wordlists) is cited for segmental areal features (nasal+voiceless stop > geminate 'follows the practice of Kalumpang'; lowered vowels in pre-penultimate prefixes; final k > glottal/lost in Karama dialects, kept in Bone Hau). No Kalumpang stress statement.

sources.note: Nothing. Lexicostatistic survey (Laskowske & Valkama trip to kecamatan Kalumpang, Sept-Oct 1985); Kalumpang divided into eight dialects; 85% similarity with the Grimeses' Kalumpang list. a full-text search for stress/accent|accent|penult: no hits. This is the 'Valkama 1987' the earlier scan named as unreachable (sil.org 403); obtained via the the Internet Archive id_ copy of the SIL reapdata PDF.
